title: Informal Conjecture on R(n;r,s) vs R'(n;r,s) near Turán density
statement_text: We clearly have $R(n; r, s) \geq R'(n; r, s)$ and we believe that this estimate should be close to an equality when $s/r$ is close to the Turán density $1 - \frac{1}{n-1}$.
context_text: For positive integers $n,r,s$ with $r>s$, an $(r,s)$-coloring of $K_N$ assigns to every edge a set of exactly $s$ colors from a palette of $r$ colors; a monochromatic $n$-clique is a set of $n$ vertices such that all edges between them share a common color. The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s)$ is the minimum $N$ such that every $(r,s)$-coloring of $K_N$ contains a monochromatic $n$-clique ($s=1$ is the classical multicolor Ramsey number). The variant $R'(n;r,s)$ is the minimum $N$ such that in every $(r,s)$-coloring of $K_N$ some color class (the graph of edges whose set contains that color) has chromatic number at least $n$; since a $K_n$ forces chromatic number $n$, $R(n;r,s)\ge R'(n;r,s)$. The authors show $R'(n;r,s)=A_{n-1}(r,s)+1$, where $A_q(r,s)$ is the maximum size of a $q$-ary code of length $r$ with minimum Hamming distance at least $s$. For fixed $n$, counting edges against the Turán number shows that $R(n;r,s)$ is bounded by a constant when $s/r\ge1-\frac{1}{n-1}+\epsilon$, whereas codes show that it grows exponentially in $r$ when $s/r\le1-\frac{1}{n-1}-\epsilon$; so the Turán density $1-\frac{1}{n-1}$ of $K_n$ is a threshold. The near-equality is confirmed for $s=r-1$ by Alon, Erdős, Gunderson and Molloy, and equality $R=R'=A_{n-1}(r,s)+1$ holds whenever suitable balanced partitions exist (each color class then being a Turán graph). The authors note that the bound $R\ge R'$ can be far from the truth in other regimes, since by the Singleton bound $A_{n-1}(r,s)\le(n-1)^{r-s+1}$ is only polynomial in $n$, while $R(n;r,s)$ can grow exponentially in $n$.
